title: Speculative kernel handoff causes cache stripe rotational offset and softmax normalization drift
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Under high-concurrency workloads with mixed batching (single-token low-latency decode requests interleaved with multi-token prefill requests), we observed deterministic but rare output drift and token misalignment. The root behavior: when the speculative kernel handoff path triggers during a prefill->decode transition, the cache stripe metadata used by the alternate kernel is rotated by one stripe index for a short window. This produces subtle column shifts in the attention buffer which, combined with an FP16 accumulation rounding boundary, leads to softmax normalization differences and divergent token logits compared to the baseline kernel. Produces reproducible semantic drift on long-context prompts and occasional off-by-one token duplication in streamed responses.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy test harness on a small dedicated pool with kernel-handoff feature flag enabled.
2) Run mixed workload: 60% short decode requests (1-3 tokens) interleaved with 40% long prefill requests (>=512 tokens), concurrency 48, sequence length skewed (prefill long before decode bursts).
3) Enable deterministic seeds and record outputs from both normal and speculative-handoff kernels for identical request sequences.
4) Compare token logits and generate diffing histogram for softmax outputs; run golden-check against baseline runtime-1.28 build.
5) Reproduce reliably with the attached repro harness (see links).
observations: - Drift appears only when mixed-precision kernels are selected on handoff path; full FP32 kernels not affected.
- The cache stripe metadata (internal stripe_offset) shows a transient +1 rotation on the alternate kernel immediately after handoff.
- Error window is ~2-6 tokens after the handoff moment; discrepancies amplify across longer attention contexts.
- CPU-side scheduling jitter correlates with increased probability of triggering the condition (higher concurrency -> higher chance).
- No GPU OOM or memory corruption observed; effects confined to logical index mapping and numeric accumulation differences.
investigation_timeline: 2026-03-01: Incident reproduced locally by QA with harness; created ticket.
2026-03-02: Initial triage: suspected kv stripe index race during kernel selection; assigned to Marco.
2026-03-04: Added additional logging around stripe_offset and kernel-selection handshake; confirmed transient +1 offset in alternate kernel's view.
2026-03-06: Cross-run diffs show softmax normalization deviates by ~1e-3 relative to baseline for affected tokens; FP16 accumulation boundary amplifies effect.
2026-03-08: Narrowed root cause to speculative kernel handoff fast-path that reuses stripe metadata without an atomic fence when switching precision panes.
2026-03-10: Prototype patch posted to PR and unit test harness updated (see links).
root_cause: Speculative kernel handoff reuses cache stripe metadata (stripe_offset pointer and stripe_epoch) without a proper memory fence and without reconciling precision-layout differences. When the alternate kernel (FP16-optimized) takes over, it interprets the stripe layout one slot off under certain scheduling interleavings. The off-by-one mapping shifts attention columns leading to altered KV alignment; combined with FP16 accumulation rounding this produces measurable softmax/logit drift.
proposed_fix: 1) Introduce an atomic handoff sequence that validates stripe_epoch and normalizes stripe_offset before any kernel begins reading the KV stripe.
2) Add a small reconciliation step that re-encodes stripe metadata for the target kernel's precision layout when handoff occurs.
3) Block speculative handoff under extremely tight prefill->decode windows until the reconciliation step completes (configurable safety guard).
4) Add unit and integration tests that simulate scheduling jitter and mixed-precision handoffs (deterministic harness included).
rollout_plan: - Merge prototype fix behind feature-flag runtime.handshake_safety_v2.
- Canary deploy to dedicated pools with low-traffic tenants for 48 hours; monitor token-diff histograms and service-level synthetic checks.
- If stable, gate-enable on 25% of hosts for 72h, then full rollout in runtime-1.30.
- Backout plan: revert feature flag and fall back to legacy conservative kernel selection if anomalies detected.
tests: - New unit tests for atomic stripe_epoch validation (fast path and slow path).
- Integration test in harness that reproduces drift with deterministic seeds.
- End-to-end comparison test against runtime-1.28 golden outputs for long-context prompts.
- Load test with mixed concurrency to validate throughput impact (<5% regression target).
notes: - This is likely related to recent optimizations around kernel speculative merging (PR #4521) but the exact mismatch is unique due to stripe layout differences.
- Priority set to P0 because customer workloads with long-context summarization can silently degrade quality.
- Engineering lead to coordinate with QA to produce reproducible corpora for downstream regression alerts in Optimize.
- Investigate whether similar metadata reuse patterns exist in other runtime subsystems (cache eviction, prefetch).
